lines.text: Flourish. Enter Lucentio and Tranio.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio, since for the great desire I had

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To see fair Padua, nursery of arts,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I am arriv’d for fruitful Lombardy,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: The pleasant garden of great Italy,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And by my father’s love and leave am arm’d

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: With his good will and thy good company,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: My trusty servant well approv’d in all,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Here let us breathe, and haply institute

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: A course of learning and ingenious studies.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Pisa, renowned for grave citizens,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Gave me my being and my father first,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: A merchant of great traffic through the world,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Vincentio, come of the Bentivolii.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Vincentio’s son, brought up in Florence,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: It shall become to serve all hopes conceiv’d,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To deck his fortune with his virtuous deeds:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And therefore, Tranio, for the time I study,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Virtue and that part of philosophy

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Will I apply that treats of happiness

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: By virtue specially to be achiev’d.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tell me thy mind; for I have Pisa left

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And am to Padua come as he that leaves

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: A shallow plash to plunge him in the deep,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And with satiety seeks to quench his thirst.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: _Mi perdonato_, gentle master mine;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I am in all affected as yourself;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Glad that you thus continue your resolve

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To suck the sweets of sweet philosophy.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Only, good master, while we do admire

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: This virtue and this moral discipline,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Let’s be no stoics nor no stocks, I pray;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Or so devote to Aristotle’s checks

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As Ovid be an outcast quite abjur’d.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Balk logic with acquaintance that you have,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And practise rhetoric in your common talk;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Music and poesy use to quicken you;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: The mathematics and the metaphysics,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Fall to them as you find your stomach serves you:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: No profit grows where is no pleasure ta’en;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: In brief, sir, study what you most affect.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Gramercies, Tranio, well dost thou advise.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: If, Biondello, thou wert come ashore,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: We could at once put us in readiness,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And take a lodging fit to entertain

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Such friends as time in Padua shall beget.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But stay awhile; what company is this?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Master, some show to welcome us to town.
[_Lucentio and Tranio stand aside._]
Enter Baptista, Katherina, Bianca, Gremio and Hortensio.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Gentlemen, importune me no farther,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For how I firmly am resolv’d you know;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: That is, not to bestow my youngest daughter

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Before I have a husband for the elder.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: If either of you both love Katherina,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Because I know you well and love you well,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Leave shall you have to court her at your pleasure.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: To cart her rather: she’s too rough for me.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: There, there, Hortensio, will you any wife?
[_To Baptista_]

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I pray you, sir, is it your will

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To make a stale of me amongst these mates?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Mates, maid! How mean you that? No mates for you,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Unless you were of gentler, milder mould.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I’ faith, sir, you shall never need to fear;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I wis it is not half way to her heart;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But if it were, doubt not her care should be

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To comb your noddle with a three-legg’d stool,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And paint your face, and use you like a fool.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: From all such devils, good Lord deliver us!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And me, too, good Lord!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Husht, master! Here’s some good pastime toward:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That wench is stark mad or wonderful froward.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But in the other’s silence do I see

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Maid’s mild behaviour and sobriety.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Peace, Tranio!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Well said, master; mum! and gaze your fill.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Gentlemen, that I may soon make good

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: What I have said,—Bianca, get you in:

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And let it not displease thee, good Bianca,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For I will love thee ne’er the less, my girl.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A pretty peat! it is best put finger in the eye, and she knew why.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Sister, content you in my discontent.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Sir, to your pleasure humbly I subscribe:

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: My books and instruments shall be my company,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: On them to look, and practise by myself.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Hark, Tranio! thou mayst hear Minerva speak.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista, will you be so strange?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sorry am I that our good will effects

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Bianca’s grief.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Why will you mew her up,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista, for this fiend of hell,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And make her bear the penance of her tongue?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Gentlemen, content ye; I am resolv’d.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Go in, Bianca.
[_Exit Bianca._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And for I know she taketh most delight

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: In music, instruments, and poetry,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Schoolmasters will I keep within my house

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Fit to instruct her youth. If you, Hortensio,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Or, Signior Gremio, you, know any such,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Prefer them hither; for to cunning men

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I will be very kind, and liberal

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: To mine own children in good bringing up;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And so, farewell. Katherina, you may stay;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For I have more to commune with Bianca.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Why, and I trust I may go too, may I not? What! shall I be appointed

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: hours, as though, belike, I knew not what to take and what to leave?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Ha!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: You may go to the devil’s dam: your gifts are so good here’s none will

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: hold you. Their love is not so great, Hortensio, but we may blow our

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: nails together, and fast it fairly out; our cake’s dough on both sides.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Farewell: yet, for the love I bear my sweet Bianca, if I can by any

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: means light on a fit man to teach her that wherein she delights, I will

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: wish him to her father.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: So will I, Signior Gremio: but a word, I pray. Though the nature of our

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: quarrel yet never brooked parle, know now, upon advice, it toucheth us

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: both,—that we may yet again have access to our fair mistress, and be

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: happy rivals in Bianca’s love,—to labour and effect one thing

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: specially.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: What’s that, I pray?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Marry, sir, to get a husband for her sister.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: A husband! a devil.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I say, a husband.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I say, a devil. Thinkest thou, Hortensio, though her father be very

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: rich, any man is so very a fool to be married to hell?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Tush, Gremio! Though it pass your patience and mine to endure her loud

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: alarums, why, man, there be good fellows in the world, and a man could

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: light on them, would take her with all faults, and money enough.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I cannot tell; but I had as lief take her dowry with this condition: to

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: be whipp’d at the high cross every morning.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Faith, as you say, there’s small choice in rotten apples. But come;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: since this bar in law makes us friends, it shall be so far forth

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: friendly maintained, till by helping Baptista’s eldest daughter to a

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: husband, we set his youngest free for a husband, and then have to’t

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: afresh. Sweet Bianca! Happy man be his dole! He that runs fastest gets

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: the ring. How say you, Signior Gremio?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I am agreed; and would I had given him the best horse in Padua to begin

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: his wooing, that would thoroughly woo her, wed her, and bed her, and

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: rid the house of her. Come on.
[_Exeunt Gremio and Hortensio._]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I pray, sir, tell me, is it possible

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That love should of a sudden take such hold?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: O Tranio! till I found it to be true,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I never thought it possible or likely;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But see, while idly I stood looking on,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I found the effect of love in idleness;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And now in plainness do confess to thee,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: That art to me as secret and as dear

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: As Anna to the Queen of Carthage was,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio, I burn, I pine, I perish, Tranio,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: If I achieve not this young modest girl.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Counsel me, Tranio, for I know thou canst:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Assist me, Tranio, for I know thou wilt.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Master, it is no time to chide you now;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Affection is not rated from the heart:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If love have touch’d you, nought remains but so:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: _Redime te captum quam queas minimo._

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Gramercies, lad; go forward; this contents;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: The rest will comfort, for thy counsel’s sound.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Master, you look’d so longly on the maid.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Perhaps you mark’d not what’s the pith of all.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: O, yes, I saw sweet beauty in her face,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Such as the daughter of Agenor had,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: That made great Jove to humble him to her hand,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: When with his knees he kiss’d the Cretan strand.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Saw you no more? mark’d you not how her sister

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Began to scold and raise up such a storm

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That mortal ears might hardly endure the din?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio, I saw her coral lips to move,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And with her breath she did perfume the air;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Sacred and sweet was all I saw in her.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Nay, then, ’tis time to stir him from his trance.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I pray, awake, sir: if you love the maid,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Bend thoughts and wits to achieve her. Thus it stands:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Her elder sister is so curst and shrewd,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That till the father rid his hands of her,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Master, your love must live a maid at home;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And therefore has he closely mew’d her up,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Because she will not be annoy’d with suitors.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Ah, Tranio, what a cruel father’s he!

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But art thou not advis’d he took some care

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To get her cunning schoolmasters to instruct her?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Ay, marry, am I, sir, and now ’tis plotted.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I have it, Tranio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Master, for my hand,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Both our inventions meet and jump in one.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tell me thine first.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: You will be schoolmaster,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And undertake the teaching of the maid:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That’s your device.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: It is: may it be done?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Not possible; for who shall bear your part

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And be in Padua here Vincentio’s son;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Keep house and ply his book, welcome his friends;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Visit his countrymen, and banquet them?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: _Basta_, content thee, for I have it full.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: We have not yet been seen in any house,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Nor can we be distinguish’d by our faces

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: For man or master: then it follows thus:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Thou shalt be master, Tranio, in my stead,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Keep house and port and servants, as I should;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I will some other be; some Florentine,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Some Neapolitan, or meaner man of Pisa.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: ’Tis hatch’d, and shall be so: Tranio, at once

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Uncase thee; take my colour’d hat and cloak.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: When Biondello comes, he waits on thee;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But I will charm him first to keep his tongue.
[_They exchange habits_]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: So had you need.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: In brief, sir, sith it your pleasure is,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And I am tied to be obedient;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: For so your father charg’d me at our parting,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ‘Be serviceable to my son,’ quoth he,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Although I think ’twas in another sense:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I am content to be Lucentio,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Because so well I love Lucentio.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio, be so, because Lucentio loves;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And let me be a slave, to achieve that maid

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Whose sudden sight hath thrall’d my wounded eye.
Enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Here comes the rogue. Sirrah, where have you been?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Where have I been? Nay, how now! where are you?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Master, has my fellow Tranio stol’n your clothes?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Or you stol’n his? or both? Pray, what’s the news?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Sirrah, come hither: ’tis no time to jest,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And therefore frame your manners to the time.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Your fellow Tranio here, to save my life,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Puts my apparel and my count’nance on,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And I for my escape have put on his;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: For in a quarrel since I came ashore

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I kill’d a man, and fear I was descried.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Wait you on him, I charge you, as becomes,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: While I make way from hence to save my life.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: You understand me?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I, sir! Ne’er a whit.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And not a jot of Tranio in your mouth:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio is changed to Lucentio.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: The better for him: would I were so too!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: So could I, faith, boy, to have the next wish after,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That Lucentio indeed had Baptista’s youngest daughter.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But, sirrah, not for my sake but your master’s, I advise

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: You use your manners discreetly in all kind of companies:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: When I am alone, why, then I am Tranio;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But in all places else your master, Lucentio.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Tranio, let’s go.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: One thing more rests, that thyself execute,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To make one among these wooers: if thou ask me why,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Sufficeth my reasons are both good and weighty.
[_Exeunt._]
[_The Presenters above speak._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: My lord, you nod; you do not mind the play.

lines.speaker: SLY
lines.text: Yes, by Saint Anne, I do. A good matter, surely: comes there any more

lines.speaker: SLY
lines.text: of it?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: My lord, ’tis but begun.

lines.speaker: SLY
lines.text: ’Tis a very excellent piece of work, madam lady: would ’twere done!
[_They sit and mark._]
Enter Petruchio and his man Grumio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Verona, for a while I take my leave,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To see my friends in Padua; but of all

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My best beloved and approved friend,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hortensio; and I trow this is his house.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here, sirrah Grumio, knock, I say.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Knock, sir? Whom should I knock? Is there any man has rebused your

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: worship?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Villain, I say, knock me here soundly.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Knock you here, sir? Why, sir, what am I, sir, that I should knock you

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: here, sir?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Villain, I say, knock me at this gate;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And rap me well, or I’ll knock your knave’s pate.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: My master is grown quarrelsome. I should knock you first,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: And then I know after who comes by the worst.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Will it not be?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Faith, sirrah, and you’ll not knock, I’ll ring it;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll try how you can sol, fa, and sing it.
[_He wrings Grumio by the ears._]

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Help, masters, help! my master is mad.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now, knock when I bid you, sirrah villain!
Enter Hortensio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: How now! what’s the matter? My old friend Grumio! and my good friend

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio! How do you all at Verona?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Signior Hortensio, come you to part the fray?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: _Con tutto il cuore ben trovato_, may I say.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: _Alla nostra casa ben venuto; molto honorato signor mio Petruchio._

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Rise, Grumio, rise: we will compound this quarrel.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Nay, ’tis no matter, sir, what he ’leges in Latin. If this be not a

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: lawful cause for me to leave his service, look you, sir, he bid me

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: knock him and rap him soundly, sir: well, was it fit for a servant to

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: use his master so; being, perhaps, for aught I see, two-and-thirty, a

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: pip out? Whom would to God I had well knock’d at first, then had not

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Grumio come by the worst.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A senseless villain! Good Hortensio,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I bade the rascal knock upon your gate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And could not get him for my heart to do it.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Knock at the gate! O heavens! Spake you not these words plain: ‘Sirrah

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: knock me here, rap me here, knock me well, and knock me soundly’? And

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: come you now with ‘knocking at the gate’?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sirrah, be gone, or talk not, I advise you.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio, patience; I am Grumio’s pledge;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Why, this’s a heavy chance ’twixt him and you,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Your ancient, trusty, pleasant servant Grumio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And tell me now, sweet friend, what happy gale

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Blows you to Padua here from old Verona?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Such wind as scatters young men through the world

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To seek their fortunes farther than at home,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where small experience grows. But in a few,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Signior Hortensio, thus it stands with me:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Antonio, my father, is deceas’d,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And I have thrust myself into this maze,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Haply to wive and thrive as best I may;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Crowns in my purse I have, and goods at home,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And so am come abroad to see the world.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio, shall I then come roundly to thee

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And wish thee to a shrewd ill-favour’d wife?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Thou’dst thank me but a little for my counsel;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And yet I’ll promise thee she shall be rich,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And very rich: but th’art too much my friend,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And I’ll not wish thee to her.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Signior Hortensio, ’twixt such friends as we

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Few words suffice; and therefore, if thou know

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: One rich enough to be Petruchio’s wife,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As wealth is burden of my wooing dance,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Be she as foul as was Florentius’ love,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As old as Sibyl, and as curst and shrewd

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As Socrates’ Xanthippe or a worse,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She moves me not, or not removes, at least,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Affection’s edge in me, were she as rough

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As are the swelling Adriatic seas:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I come to wive it wealthily in Padua;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If wealthily, then happily in Padua.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Nay, look you, sir, he tells you flatly what his mind is: why, give him

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: gold enough and marry him to a puppet or an aglet-baby; or an old trot

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: with ne’er a tooth in her head, though she have as many diseases as

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: two-and-fifty horses: why, nothing comes amiss, so money comes withal.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio, since we are stepp’d thus far in,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I will continue that I broach’d in jest.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I can, Petruchio, help thee to a wife

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: With wealth enough, and young and beauteous;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Brought up as best becomes a gentlewoman:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Her only fault,—and that is faults enough,—

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Is, that she is intolerable curst,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And shrewd and froward, so beyond all measure,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That, were my state far worser than it is,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I would not wed her for a mine of gold.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hortensio, peace! thou know’st not gold’s effect:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Tell me her father’s name, and ’tis enough;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For I will board her, though she chide as loud

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As thunder when the clouds in autumn crack.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Her father is Baptista Minola,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: An affable and courteous gentleman;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Her name is Katherina Minola,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Renown’d in Padua for her scolding tongue.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I know her father, though I know not her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And he knew my deceased father well.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will not sleep, Hortensio, till I see her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And therefore let me be thus bold with you,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To give you over at this first encounter,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Unless you will accompany me thither.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I pray you, sir, let him go while the humour lasts. O’ my word, and she

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: knew him as well as I do, she would think scolding would do little good

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: upon him. She may perhaps call him half a score knaves or so; why,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: that’s nothing; and he begin once, he’ll rail in his rope-tricks. I’ll

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: tell you what, sir, and she stand him but a little, he will throw a

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: figure in her face, and so disfigure her with it that she shall have no

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: more eyes to see withal than a cat. You know him not, sir.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Tarry, Petruchio, I must go with thee,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For in Baptista’s keep my treasure is:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: He hath the jewel of my life in hold,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: His youngest daughter, beautiful Bianca,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And her withholds from me and other more,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Suitors to her and rivals in my love;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Supposing it a thing impossible,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For those defects I have before rehears’d,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That ever Katherina will be woo’d:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Therefore this order hath Baptista ta’en,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That none shall have access unto Bianca

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Till Katherine the curst have got a husband.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Katherine the curst!

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: A title for a maid of all titles the worst.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Now shall my friend Petruchio do me grace,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And offer me disguis’d in sober robes,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To old Baptista as a schoolmaster

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Well seen in music, to instruct Bianca;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That so I may, by this device at least

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Have leave and leisure to make love to her,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And unsuspected court her by herself.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Here’s no knavery! See, to beguile the old folks, how the young folks

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: lay their heads together!
Enter Gremio and Lucentio disguised, with books under his arm.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Master, master, look about you: who goes there, ha?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Peace, Grumio! It is the rival of my love. Petruchio, stand by awhile.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: A proper stripling, and an amorous!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: O! very well; I have perus’d the note.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hark you, sir; I’ll have them very fairly bound:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: All books of love, see that at any hand,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And see you read no other lectures to her.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: You understand me. Over and beside

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista’s liberality,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I’ll mend it with a largess. Take your papers too,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And let me have them very well perfum’d;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: For she is sweeter than perfume itself

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: To whom they go to. What will you read to her?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Whate’er I read to her, I’ll plead for you,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: As for my patron, stand you so assur’d,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: As firmly as yourself were still in place;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Yea, and perhaps with more successful words

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Than you, unless you were a scholar, sir.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: O! this learning, what a thing it is.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: O! this woodcock, what an ass it is.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Peace, sirrah!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Grumio, mum! God save you, Signior Gremio!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And you are well met, Signior Hortensio.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Trow you whither I am going? To Baptista Minola.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I promis’d to enquire carefully

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: About a schoolmaster for the fair Bianca;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And by good fortune I have lighted well

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: On this young man; for learning and behaviour

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Fit for her turn, well read in poetry

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And other books, good ones, I warrant ye.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: ’Tis well; and I have met a gentleman

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Hath promis’d me to help me to another,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: A fine musician to instruct our mistress:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: So shall I no whit be behind in duty

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To fair Bianca, so belov’d of me.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Belov’d of me, and that my deeds shall prove.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: And that his bags shall prove.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Gremio, ’tis now no time to vent our love:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Listen to me, and if you speak me fair,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I’ll tell you news indifferent good for either.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Here is a gentleman whom by chance I met,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Upon agreement from us to his liking,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Will undertake to woo curst Katherine;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Yea, and to marry her, if her dowry please.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: So said, so done, is well.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hortensio, have you told him all her faults?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I know she is an irksome brawling scold;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If that be all, masters, I hear no harm.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: No, say’st me so, friend? What countryman?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Born in Verona, old Antonio’s son.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My father dead, my fortune lives for me;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And I do hope good days and long to see.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: O sir, such a life, with such a wife, were strange!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But if you have a stomach, to’t a God’s name;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: You shall have me assisting you in all.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But will you woo this wild-cat?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Will I live?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Will he woo her? Ay, or I’ll hang her.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why came I hither but to that intent?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Think you a little din can daunt mine ears?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Have I not in my time heard lions roar?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Have I not heard the sea, puff’d up with winds,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Rage like an angry boar chafed with sweat?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Have I not heard great ordnance in the field,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And heaven’s artillery thunder in the skies?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Have I not in a pitched battle heard

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Loud ’larums, neighing steeds, and trumpets’ clang?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And do you tell me of a woman’s tongue,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That gives not half so great a blow to hear

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As will a chestnut in a farmer’s fire?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Tush, tush! fear boys with bugs.
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: For he fears none.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hortensio, hark:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: This gentleman is happily arriv’d,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: My mind presumes, for his own good and yours.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I promis’d we would be contributors,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And bear his charge of wooing, whatsoe’er.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And so we will, provided that he win her.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I would I were as sure of a good dinner.
Enter Tranio brave, and Biondello.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Gentlemen, God save you! If I may be bold,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Tell me, I beseech you, which is the readiest way

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To the house of Signior Baptista Minola?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: He that has the two fair daughters; is’t he you mean?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Even he, Biondello!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hark you, sir, you mean not her to—

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Perhaps him and her, sir; what have you to do?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Not her that chides, sir, at any hand, I pray.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I love no chiders, sir. Biondello, let’s away.
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Well begun, Tranio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sir, a word ere you go.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Are you a suitor to the maid you talk of, yea or no?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And if I be, sir, is it any offence?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: No; if without more words you will get you hence.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Why, sir, I pray, are not the streets as free

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: For me as for you?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But so is not she.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: For what reason, I beseech you?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: For this reason, if you’ll know,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That she’s the choice love of Signior Gremio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That she’s the chosen of Signior Hortensio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Softly, my masters! If you be gentlemen,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Do me this right; hear me with patience.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Baptista is a noble gentleman,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To whom my father is not all unknown;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And were his daughter fairer than she is,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: She may more suitors have, and me for one.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Fair Leda’s daughter had a thousand wooers;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Then well one more may fair Bianca have;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And so she shall: Lucentio shall make one,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Though Paris came in hope to speed alone.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: What, this gentleman will out-talk us all.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Sir, give him head; I know he’ll prove a jade.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hortensio, to what end are all these words?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sir, let me be so bold as ask you,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Did you yet ever see Baptista’s daughter?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: No, sir, but hear I do that he hath two,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: The one as famous for a scolding tongue

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As is the other for beauteous modesty.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sir, sir, the first’s for me; let her go by.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Yea, leave that labour to great Hercules,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And let it be more than Alcides’ twelve.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sir, understand you this of me, in sooth:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The youngest daughter, whom you hearken for,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her father keeps from all access of suitors,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And will not promise her to any man

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Until the elder sister first be wed;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The younger then is free, and not before.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If it be so, sir, that you are the man

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Must stead us all, and me amongst the rest;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And if you break the ice, and do this feat,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Achieve the elder, set the younger free

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: For our access, whose hap shall be to have her

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Will not so graceless be to be ingrate.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sir, you say well, and well you do conceive;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And since you do profess to be a suitor,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: You must, as we do, gratify this gentleman,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To whom we all rest generally beholding.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Sir, I shall not be slack; in sign whereof,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Please ye we may contrive this afternoon,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And quaff carouses to our mistress’ health;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And do as adversaries do in law,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Strive mightily, but eat and drink as friends.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO, BIONDELLO
lines.text: O excellent motion! Fellows, let’s be gone.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: The motion’s good indeed, and be it so:—

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio, I shall be your _ben venuto_.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Padua. A room in Baptista’s house.

lines.text: Enter Katherina and Bianca.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Good sister, wrong me not, nor wrong yourself,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: To make a bondmaid and a slave of me;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: That I disdain; but for these other gawds,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Unbind my hands, I’ll pull them off myself,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Yea, all my raiment, to my petticoat;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Or what you will command me will I do,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: So well I know my duty to my elders.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Of all thy suitors here I charge thee tell

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Whom thou lov’st best: see thou dissemble not.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Believe me, sister, of all the men alive

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I never yet beheld that special face

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Which I could fancy more than any other.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Minion, thou liest. Is’t not Hortensio?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: If you affect him, sister, here I swear

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I’ll plead for you myself but you shall have him.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: O! then, belike, you fancy riches more:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: You will have Gremio to keep you fair.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Is it for him you do envy me so?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Nay, then you jest; and now I well perceive

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: You have but jested with me all this while:

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I prithee, sister Kate, untie my hands.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If that be jest, then all the rest was so.
[_Strikes her._]
Enter Baptista.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, how now, dame! Whence grows this insolence?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Bianca, stand aside. Poor girl! she weeps.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Go ply thy needle; meddle not with her.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For shame, thou hilding of a devilish spirit,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why dost thou wrong her that did ne’er wrong thee?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: When did she cross thee with a bitter word?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Her silence flouts me, and I’ll be reveng’d.
[_Flies after Bianca._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: What! in my sight? Bianca, get thee in.
[_Exit Bianca._]

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What! will you not suffer me? Nay, now I see

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: She is your treasure, she must have a husband;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I must dance bare-foot on her wedding-day,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And, for your love to her, lead apes in hell.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Talk not to me: I will go sit and weep

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Till I can find occasion of revenge.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Was ever gentleman thus griev’d as I?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But who comes here?
Enter Gremio, with Lucentio in the habit of a mean man; Petruchio, with Hortensio as a musician; and Tranio, with Biondello bearing a lute and books.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Good morrow, neighbour Baptista.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Good morrow, neighbour Gremio. God save you, gentlemen!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And you, good sir! Pray, have you not a daughter

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Call’d Katherina, fair and virtuous?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I have a daughter, sir, call’d Katherina.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: You are too blunt: go to it orderly.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You wrong me, Signior Gremio: give me leave.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I am a gentleman of Verona, sir,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That, hearing of her beauty and her wit,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her affability and bashful modesty,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her wondrous qualities and mild behaviour,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Am bold to show myself a forward guest

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Within your house, to make mine eye the witness

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Of that report which I so oft have heard.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And, for an entrance to my entertainment,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I do present you with a man of mine,
[_Presenting Hortensio._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Cunning in music and the mathematics,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To instruct her fully in those sciences,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Whereof I know she is not ignorant.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Accept of him, or else you do me wrong:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: His name is Licio, born in Mantua.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Y’are welcome, sir, and he for your good sake;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But for my daughter Katherine, this I know,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: She is not for your turn, the more my grief.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I see you do not mean to part with her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Or else you like not of my company.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Mistake me not; I speak but as I find.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Whence are you, sir? What may I call your name?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Petruchio is my name, Antonio’s son;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A man well known throughout all Italy.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I know him well: you are welcome for his sake.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Saving your tale, Petruchio, I pray,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Let us, that are poor petitioners, speak too.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Backare! you are marvellous forward.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O, pardon me, Signior Gremio; I would fain be doing.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I doubt it not, sir; but you will curse your wooing. Neighbour, this is

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: a gift very grateful, I am sure of it. To express the like kindness,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: myself, that have been more kindly beholding to you than any, freely

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: give unto you this young scholar,
[_Presenting Lucentio._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: that has been long studying at Rheims; as cunning in Greek, Latin, and

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: other languages, as the other in music and mathematics. His name is

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Cambio; pray accept his service.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: A thousand thanks, Signior Gremio; welcome, good Cambio.
[_To Tranio._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But, gentle sir, methinks you walk like a stranger. May I be so bold to

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: know the cause of your coming?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Pardon me, sir, the boldness is mine own,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That, being a stranger in this city here,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Do make myself a suitor to your daughter,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Unto Bianca, fair and virtuous.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Nor is your firm resolve unknown to me,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: In the preferment of the eldest sister.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: This liberty is all that I request,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That, upon knowledge of my parentage,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I may have welcome ’mongst the rest that woo,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And free access and favour as the rest:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And, toward the education of your daughters,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I here bestow a simple instrument,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And this small packet of Greek and Latin books:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If you accept them, then their worth is great.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Lucentio is your name, of whence, I pray?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of Pisa, sir; son to Vincentio.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: A mighty man of Pisa: by report

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I know him well: you are very welcome, sir.
[_To Hortensio_.]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Take you the lute,
[_To Lucentio_.]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: and you the set of books;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: You shall go see your pupils presently.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Holla, within!
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Sirrah, lead these gentlemen

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: To my daughters, and tell them both

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: These are their tutors: bid them use them well.
[_Exeunt Servant with Hortensio, Lucentio and Biondello._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: We will go walk a little in the orchard,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And then to dinner. You are passing welcome,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And so I pray you all to think yourselves.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista, my business asketh haste,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And every day I cannot come to woo.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You knew my father well, and in him me,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Left solely heir to all his lands and goods,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Which I have bettered rather than decreas’d:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Then tell me, if I get your daughter’s love,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What dowry shall I have with her to wife?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: After my death, the one half of my lands,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And in possession twenty thousand crowns.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And, for that dowry, I’ll assure her of

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her widowhood, be it that she survive me,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: In all my lands and leases whatsoever.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Let specialities be therefore drawn between us,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That covenants may be kept on either hand.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Ay, when the special thing is well obtain’d,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: That is, her love; for that is all in all.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, that is nothing; for I tell you, father,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I am as peremptory as she proud-minded;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And where two raging fires meet together,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: They do consume the thing that feeds their fury:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Though little fire grows great with little wind,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Yet extreme gusts will blow out fire and all;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: So I to her, and so she yields to me;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For I am rough and woo not like a babe.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Well mayst thou woo, and happy be thy speed!

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But be thou arm’d for some unhappy words.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Ay, to the proof, as mountains are for winds,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That shake not though they blow perpetually.
Re-enter Hortensio, with his head broke.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: How now, my friend! Why dost thou look so pale?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For fear, I promise you, if I look pale.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: What, will my daughter prove a good musician?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I think she’ll sooner prove a soldier:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Iron may hold with her, but never lutes.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, then thou canst not break her to the lute?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Why, no; for she hath broke the lute to me.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I did but tell her she mistook her frets,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And bow’d her hand to teach her fingering;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: When, with a most impatient devilish spirit,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: ‘Frets, call you these?’ quoth she ‘I’ll fume with them’;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And with that word she struck me on the head,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And through the instrument my pate made way;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And there I stood amazed for a while,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: As on a pillory, looking through the lute;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: While she did call me rascal fiddler,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And twangling Jack, with twenty such vile terms,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: As had she studied to misuse me so.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now, by the world, it is a lusty wench!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I love her ten times more than e’er I did:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O! how I long to have some chat with her!
[_To Hortensio_.]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Well, go with me, and be not so discomfited;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Proceed in practice with my younger daughter;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: She’s apt to learn, and thankful for good turns.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Signior Petruchio, will you go with us,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Or shall I send my daughter Kate to you?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I pray you do.
[_Exeunt Baptista, Gremio, Tranio and Hortensio._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will attend her here,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And woo her with some spirit when she comes.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Say that she rail; why, then I’ll tell her plain

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She sings as sweetly as a nightingale:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Say that she frown; I’ll say she looks as clear

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As morning roses newly wash’d with dew:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Say she be mute, and will not speak a word;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Then I’ll commend her volubility,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And say she uttereth piercing eloquence:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If she do bid me pack, I’ll give her thanks,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As though she bid me stay by her a week:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If she deny to wed, I’ll crave the day

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: When I shall ask the banns, and when be married.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But here she comes; and now, Petruchio, speak.
Enter Katherina.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Good morrow, Kate; for that’s your name, I hear.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Well have you heard, but something hard of hearing:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: They call me Katherine that do talk of me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You lie, in faith, for you are call’d plain Kate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And bonny Kate, and sometimes Kate the curst;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But, Kate, the prettiest Kate in Christendom,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Kate of Kate Hall, my super-dainty Kate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For dainties are all Kates, and therefore, Kate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Take this of me, Kate of my consolation;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hearing thy mildness prais’d in every town,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thy virtues spoke of, and thy beauty sounded,—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Yet not so deeply as to thee belongs,—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Myself am mov’d to woo thee for my wife.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Mov’d! in good time: let him that mov’d you hither

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Remove you hence. I knew you at the first,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: You were a moveable.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, what’s a moveable?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A joint-stool.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou hast hit it: come, sit on me.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Asses are made to bear, and so are you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Women are made to bear, and so are you.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: No such jade as bear you, if me you mean.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Alas! good Kate, I will not burden thee;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For, knowing thee to be but young and light,—

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Too light for such a swain as you to catch;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And yet as heavy as my weight should be.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Should be! should buz!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Well ta’en, and like a buzzard.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O, slow-wing’d turtle! shall a buzzard take thee?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Ay, for a turtle, as he takes a buzzard.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, come, you wasp; i’ faith, you are too angry.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If I be waspish, best beware my sting.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My remedy is then to pluck it out.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Ay, if the fool could find it where it lies.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Who knows not where a wasp does wear his sting?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: In his tail.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: In his tongue.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Whose tongue?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Yours, if you talk of tales; and so farewell.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What! with my tongue in your tail? Nay, come again,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Good Kate; I am a gentleman.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That I’ll try.
[_Striking him._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I swear I’ll cuff you if you strike again.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: So may you lose your arms:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If you strike me, you are no gentleman;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And if no gentleman, why then no arms.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A herald, Kate? O! put me in thy books.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What is your crest? a coxcomb?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A combless cock, so Kate will be my hen.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: No cock of mine; you crow too like a craven.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, come, Kate, come; you must not look so sour.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: It is my fashion when I see a crab.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, here’s no crab, and therefore look not sour.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: There is, there is.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Then show it me.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Had I a glass I would.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What, you mean my face?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Well aim’d of such a young one.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now, by Saint George, I am too young for you.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Yet you are wither’d.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Tis with cares.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I care not.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, hear you, Kate: in sooth, you ’scape not so.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I chafe you, if I tarry; let me go.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: No, not a whit; I find you passing gentle.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Twas told me you were rough, and coy, and sullen,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And now I find report a very liar;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For thou art pleasant, gamesome, passing courteous,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But slow in speech, yet sweet as spring-time flowers.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou canst not frown, thou canst not look askance,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nor bite the lip, as angry wenches will,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nor hast thou pleasure to be cross in talk;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But thou with mildness entertain’st thy wooers;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: With gentle conference, soft and affable.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why does the world report that Kate doth limp?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O sland’rous world! Kate like the hazel-twig

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Is straight and slender, and as brown in hue

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As hazel-nuts, and sweeter than the kernels.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O! let me see thee walk: thou dost not halt.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Go, fool, and whom thou keep’st command.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Did ever Dian so become a grove

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As Kate this chamber with her princely gait?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O! be thou Dian, and let her be Kate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And then let Kate be chaste, and Dian sportful!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Where did you study all this goodly speech?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It is extempore, from my mother-wit.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A witty mother! witless else her son.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Am I not wise?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Yes; keep you warm.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Marry, so I mean, sweet Katherine, in thy bed;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And therefore, setting all this chat aside,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thus in plain terms: your father hath consented

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That you shall be my wife your dowry ’greed on;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And will you, nill you, I will marry you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now, Kate, I am a husband for your turn;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For, by this light, whereby I see thy beauty,—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thy beauty that doth make me like thee well,—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou must be married to no man but me;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For I am he am born to tame you, Kate,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And bring you from a wild Kate to a Kate

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Conformable as other household Kates.
Re-enter Baptista, Gremio and Tranio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here comes your father. Never make denial;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I must and will have Katherine to my wife.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now, Signior Petruchio, how speed you with my daughter?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How but well, sir? how but well?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It were impossible I should speed amiss.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, how now, daughter Katherine, in your dumps?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Call you me daughter? Now I promise you

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: You have show’d a tender fatherly regard

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To wish me wed to one half lunatic,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A mad-cap ruffian and a swearing Jack,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That thinks with oaths to face the matter out.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Father, ’tis thus: yourself and all the world

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That talk’d of her have talk’d amiss of her:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If she be curst, it is for policy,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For she’s not froward, but modest as the dove;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She is not hot, but temperate as the morn;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For patience she will prove a second Grissel,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And Roman Lucrece for her chastity;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And to conclude, we have ’greed so well together

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That upon Sunday is the wedding-day.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I’ll see thee hang’d on Sunday first.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hark, Petruchio; she says she’ll see thee hang’d first.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Is this your speeding? Nay, then good-night our part!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Be patient, gentlemen. I choose her for myself;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If she and I be pleas’d, what’s that to you?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Tis bargain’d ’twixt us twain, being alone,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That she shall still be curst in company.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I tell you, ’tis incredible to believe

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How much she loves me: O! the kindest Kate

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She hung about my neck, and kiss on kiss

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She vied so fast, protesting oath on oath,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That in a twink she won me to her love.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O! you are novices: ’tis a world to see,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How tame, when men and women are alone,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A meacock wretch can make the curstest shrew.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Give me thy hand, Kate; I will unto Venice,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To buy apparel ’gainst the wedding-day.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Provide the feast, father, and bid the guests;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will be sure my Katherine shall be fine.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I know not what to say; but give me your hands.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: God send you joy, Petruchio! ’Tis a match.

lines.speaker: GREMIO, TRANIO
lines.text: Amen, say we; we will be witnesses.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Father, and wife, and gentlemen, adieu.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will to Venice; Sunday comes apace;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: We will have rings and things, and fine array;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And kiss me, Kate; we will be married o’ Sunday.
[_Exeunt Petruchio and Katherina, severally._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Was ever match clapp’d up so suddenly?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Faith, gentlemen, now I play a merchant’s part,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And venture madly on a desperate mart.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Twas a commodity lay fretting by you;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Twill bring you gain, or perish on the seas.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: The gain I seek is, quiet in the match.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: No doubt but he hath got a quiet catch.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But now, Baptista, to your younger daughter:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Now is the day we long have looked for;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I am your neighbour, and was suitor first.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And I am one that love Bianca more

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Than words can witness or your thoughts can guess.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Youngling, thou canst not love so dear as I.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Greybeard, thy love doth freeze.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But thine doth fry.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Skipper, stand back; ’tis age that nourisheth.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But youth in ladies’ eyes that flourisheth.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Content you, gentlemen; I’ll compound this strife:

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: ’Tis deeds must win the prize, and he of both

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: That can assure my daughter greatest dower

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Shall have my Bianca’s love.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Say, Signior Gremio, what can you assure her?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: First, as you know, my house within the city

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Is richly furnished with plate and gold:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Basins and ewers to lave her dainty hands;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: My hangings all of Tyrian tapestry;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: In ivory coffers I have stuff’d my crowns;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: In cypress chests my arras counterpoints,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Costly apparel, tents, and canopies,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Fine linen, Turkey cushions boss’d with pearl,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Valance of Venice gold in needlework;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Pewter and brass, and all things that belong

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: To house or housekeeping: then, at my farm

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I have a hundred milch-kine to the pail,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Six score fat oxen standing in my stalls,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And all things answerable to this portion.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Myself am struck in years, I must confess;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And if I die tomorrow this is hers,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: If whilst I live she will be only mine.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That ‘only’ came well in. Sir, list to me:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I am my father’s heir and only son;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If I may have your daughter to my wife,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I’ll leave her houses three or four as good

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Within rich Pisa’s walls as anyone

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Old Signior Gremio has in Padua;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Besides two thousand ducats by the year

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of fruitful land, all which shall be her jointure.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: What, have I pinch’d you, Signior Gremio?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Two thousand ducats by the year of land!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: My land amounts not to so much in all:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That she shall have, besides an argosy

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That now is lying in Marseilles’ road.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: What, have I chok’d you with an argosy?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Gremio, ’tis known my father hath no less

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Than three great argosies, besides two galliasses,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And twelve tight galleys; these I will assure her,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And twice as much, whate’er thou offer’st next.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Nay, I have offer’d all; I have no more;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And she can have no more than all I have;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: If you like me, she shall have me and mine.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Why, then the maid is mine from all the world,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: By your firm promise; Gremio is out-vied.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I must confess your offer is the best;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And let your father make her the assurance,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: She is your own; else, you must pardon me;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: If you should die before him, where’s her dower?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That’s but a cavil; he is old, I young.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And may not young men die as well as old?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Well, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I am thus resolv’d. On Sunday next, you know,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: My daughter Katherine is to be married;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now, on the Sunday following, shall Bianca

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Be bride to you, if you make this assurance;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: If not, to Signior Gremio.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And so I take my leave, and thank you both.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Adieu, good neighbour.
[_Exit Baptista._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Now, I fear thee not:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Sirrah young gamester, your father were a fool

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: To give thee all, and in his waning age

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Set foot under thy table. Tut! a toy!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: An old Italian fox is not so kind, my boy.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: A vengeance on your crafty wither’d hide!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Yet I have fac’d it with a card of ten.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis in my head to do my master good:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I see no reason but suppos’d Lucentio

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Must get a father, call’d suppos’d Vincentio;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And that’s a wonder: fathers commonly

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Do get their children; but in this case of wooing

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: A child shall get a sire, if I fail not of my cunning.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Padua. A room in Baptista’s house.

lines.text: Enter Lucentio, Hortensio and Bianca.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Fiddler, forbear; you grow too forward, sir.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Have you so soon forgot the entertainment

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Her sister Katherine welcome’d you withal?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: But, wrangling pedant, this is

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: The patroness of heavenly harmony:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Then give me leave to have prerogative;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And when in music we have spent an hour,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Your lecture shall have leisure for as much.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Preposterous ass, that never read so far

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To know the cause why music was ordain’d!

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Was it not to refresh the mind of man

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: After his studies or his usual pain?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Then give me leave to read philosophy,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And while I pause serve in your harmony.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sirrah, I will not bear these braves of thine.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Why, gentlemen, you do me double wrong,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: To strive for that which resteth in my choice.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I am no breeching scholar in the schools,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I’ll not be tied to hours nor ’pointed times,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: But learn my lessons as I please myself.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: And, to cut off all strife, here sit we down;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Take you your instrument, play you the whiles;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: His lecture will be done ere you have tun’d.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: You’ll leave his lecture when I am in tune?
[_Retires._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: That will be never: tune your instrument.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Where left we last?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Here, madam:—

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: _Hic ibat Simois; hic est Sigeia tellus;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Hic steterat Priami regia celsa senis._

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Construe them.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: _Hic ibat_, as I told you before, _Simois_, I am Lucentio, _hic est_,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: son unto Vincentio of Pisa, _Sigeia tellus_, disguised thus to get your

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: love, _Hic steterat_, and that Lucentio that comes a-wooing, _Priami_,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: is my man Tranio, _regia_, bearing my port, _celsa senis_, that we

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: might beguile the old pantaloon.
[_Returning._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Madam, my instrument’s in tune.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Let’s hear.—
[Hortensio _plays._]

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: O fie! the treble jars.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Spit in the hole, man, and tune again.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Now let me see if I can construe it: _Hic ibat Simois_, I know you not;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _hic est Sigeia tellus_, I trust you not; _Hic steterat Priami_, take

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: heed he hear us not; _regia_, presume not; _celsa senis_, despair not.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Madam, ’tis now in tune.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: All but the base.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: The base is right; ’tis the base knave that jars.
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: How fiery and forward our pedant is!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Now, for my life, the knave doth court my love:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Pedascule, I’ll watch you better yet.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: In time I may believe, yet I mistrust.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Mistrust it not; for sure, Æacides

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Was Ajax, call’d so from his grandfather.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I must believe my master; else, I promise you,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: I should be arguing still upon that doubt;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: But let it rest. Now, Licio, to you.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Good master, take it not unkindly, pray,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: That I have been thus pleasant with you both.
[_To Lucentio_]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: You may go walk and give me leave a while;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: My lessons make no music in three parts.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Are you so formal, sir? Well, I must wait,
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
