lines.text: And watch withal; for, but I be deceiv’d,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Our fine musician groweth amorous.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Madam, before you touch the instrument,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To learn the order of my fingering,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I must begin with rudiments of art;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To teach you gamut in a briefer sort,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: More pleasant, pithy, and effectual,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Than hath been taught by any of my trade:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And there it is in writing, fairly drawn.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Why, I am past my gamut long ago.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Yet read the gamut of Hortensio.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _Gamut_ I am, the ground of all accord,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _A re_, to plead Hortensio’s passion;

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _B mi_, Bianca, take him for thy lord,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _C fa ut_, that loves with all affection:

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _D sol re_, one clef, two notes have I

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: _E la mi_, show pity or I die.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Call you this gamut? Tut, I like it not:

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Old fashions please me best; I am not so nice,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: To change true rules for odd inventions.
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Mistress, your father prays you leave your books,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: And help to dress your sister’s chamber up:

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: You know tomorrow is the wedding-day.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Farewell, sweet masters, both: I must be gone.
[_Exeunt Bianca and Servant._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Faith, mistress, then I have no cause to stay.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: But I have cause to pry into this pedant:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Methinks he looks as though he were in love.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Yet if thy thoughts, Bianca, be so humble

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To cast thy wand’ring eyes on every stale,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Seize thee that list: if once I find thee ranging,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Hortensio will be quit with thee by changing.
[_Exit._]
Enter Baptista, Gremio, Tranio, Katherina, Bianca, Lucentio and Attendants.

BAPTISTA.  [_To Tranio_.] Signior Lucentio, this is the ’pointed day That Katherine and Petruchio should be married, And yet we hear not of our son-in-law. What will be said? What mockery will it be To want the bridegroom when the priest attends To speak the ceremonial rites of marriage! What says Lucentio to this shame of ours?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: No shame but mine; I must, forsooth, be forc’d

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To give my hand, oppos’d against my heart,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Unto a mad-brain rudesby, full of spleen;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Who woo’d in haste and means to wed at leisure.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I told you, I, he was a frantic fool,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Hiding his bitter jests in blunt behaviour;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And to be noted for a merry man,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: He’ll woo a thousand, ’point the day of marriage,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Make friends, invite, and proclaim the banns;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Yet never means to wed where he hath woo’d.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Now must the world point at poor Katherine,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And say ‘Lo! there is mad Petruchio’s wife,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If it would please him come and marry her.’

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Patience, good Katherine, and Baptista too.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Upon my life, Petruchio means but well,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Whatever fortune stays him from his word:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Though he be blunt, I know him passing wise;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Though he be merry, yet withal he’s honest.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Would Katherine had never seen him though!
[_Exit weeping, followed by Bianca and others._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Go, girl, I cannot blame thee now to weep,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For such an injury would vex a very saint;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Much more a shrew of thy impatient humour.
Enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Master, master! News! old news, and such news as you never heard of!

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Is it new and old too? How may that be?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Why, is it not news to hear of Petruchio’s coming?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Is he come?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Why, no, sir.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: He is coming.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: When will he be here?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: When he stands where I am and sees you there.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But say, what to thine old news?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Why, Petruchio is coming, in a new hat and an old jerkin; a pair of old

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: breeches thrice turned; a pair of boots that have been candle-cases,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: one buckled, another laced; an old rusty sword ta’en out of the town

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: armoury, with a broken hilt, and chapeless; with two broken points: his

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: horse hipped with an old mothy saddle and stirrups of no kindred;

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: besides, possessed with the glanders and like to mose in the chine;

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: troubled with the lampass, infected with the fashions, full of

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: windgalls, sped with spavins, rayed with the yellows, past cure of the

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: fives, stark spoiled with the staggers, begnawn with the bots, swayed

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: in the back and shoulder-shotten; near-legged before, and with a

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: half-checked bit, and a head-stall of sheep’s leather, which, being

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: restrained to keep him from stumbling, hath been often burst, and now

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: repaired with knots; one girth six times pieced, and a woman’s crupper

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: of velure, which hath two letters for her name fairly set down in

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: studs, and here and there pieced with pack-thread.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Who comes with him?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: O, sir! his lackey, for all the world caparisoned like the horse; with

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: a linen stock on one leg and a kersey boot-hose on the other, gartered

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: with a red and blue list; an old hat, and the humour of forty fancies

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: prick’d in’t for a feather: a monster, a very monster in apparel, and

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: not like a Christian footboy or a gentleman’s lackey.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis some odd humour pricks him to this fashion;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Yet oftentimes he goes but mean-apparell’d.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I am glad he’s come, howsoe’er he comes.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Why, sir, he comes not.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Didst thou not say he comes?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Who? that Petruchio came?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Ay, that Petruchio came.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: No, sir; I say his horse comes, with him on his back.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, that’s all one.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Nay, by Saint Jamy,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I hold you a penny,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: A horse and a man

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Is more than one,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: And yet not many.
Enter Petruchio and Grumio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, where be these gallants? Who is at home?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: You are welcome, sir.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And yet I come not well.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And yet you halt not.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Not so well apparell’d as I wish you were.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Were it better, I should rush in thus.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But where is Kate? Where is my lovely bride?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How does my father? Gentles, methinks you frown;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And wherefore gaze this goodly company,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As if they saw some wondrous monument,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Some comet or unusual prodigy?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, sir, you know this is your wedding-day:

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: First were we sad, fearing you would not come;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now sadder, that you come so unprovided.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Fie! doff this habit, shame to your estate,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: An eye-sore to our solemn festival.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And tell us what occasion of import

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Hath all so long detain’d you from your wife,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And sent you hither so unlike yourself?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Tedious it were to tell, and harsh to hear;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sufficeth I am come to keep my word,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Though in some part enforced to digress;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Which at more leisure I will so excuse

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As you shall well be satisfied withal.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But where is Kate? I stay too long from her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The morning wears, ’tis time we were at church.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: See not your bride in these unreverent robes;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Go to my chamber, put on clothes of mine.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Not I, believe me: thus I’ll visit her.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But thus, I trust, you will not marry her.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Good sooth, even thus; therefore ha’ done with words;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To me she’s married, not unto my clothes.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Could I repair what she will wear in me

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As I can change these poor accoutrements,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Twere well for Kate and better for myself.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But what a fool am I to chat with you

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: When I should bid good morrow to my bride,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And seal the title with a lovely kiss!
[_Exeunt Petruchio, Grumio and Biondello._]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: He hath some meaning in his mad attire.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: We will persuade him, be it possible,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To put on better ere he go to church.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I’ll after him and see the event of this.
[_Exeunt Baptista, Gremio and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But, sir, to love concerneth us to add

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Her father’s liking; which to bring to pass,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As I before imparted to your worship,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I am to get a man,—whate’er he be

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: It skills not much; we’ll fit him to our turn,—

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And he shall be Vincentio of Pisa,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And make assurance here in Padua,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of greater sums than I have promised.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: So shall you quietly enjoy your hope,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And marry sweet Bianca with consent.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Were it not that my fellow schoolmaster

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Doth watch Bianca’s steps so narrowly,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: ’Twere good, methinks, to steal our marriage;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Which once perform’d, let all the world say no,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I’ll keep mine own despite of all the world.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That by degrees we mean to look into,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And watch our vantage in this business.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: We’ll over-reach the greybeard, Gremio,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: The narrow-prying father, Minola,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: The quaint musician, amorous Licio;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: All for my master’s sake, Lucentio.
Re-enter Gremio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Signior Gremio, came you from the church?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: As willingly as e’er I came from school.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And is the bride and bridegroom coming home?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: A bridegroom, say you? ’Tis a groom indeed,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: A grumbling groom, and that the girl shall find.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Curster than she? Why, ’tis impossible.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Why, he’s a devil, a devil, a very fiend.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Why, she’s a devil, a devil, the devil’s dam.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Tut! she’s a lamb, a dove, a fool, to him.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I’ll tell you, Sir Lucentio: when the priest

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Should ask if Katherine should be his wife,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: ’Ay, by gogs-wouns’ quoth he, and swore so loud

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That, all amaz’d, the priest let fall the book;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And as he stoop’d again to take it up,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: The mad-brain’d bridegroom took him such a cuff

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That down fell priest and book, and book and priest:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: ‘Now take them up,’ quoth he ‘if any list.’

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: What said the wench, when he rose again?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Trembled and shook, for why, he stamp’d and swore

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: As if the vicar meant to cozen him.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But after many ceremonies done,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: He calls for wine: ‘A health!’ quoth he, as if

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: He had been abroad, carousing to his mates

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: After a storm; quaff’d off the muscadel,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And threw the sops all in the sexton’s face,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Having no other reason

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: But that his beard grew thin and hungerly

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And seem’d to ask him sops as he was drinking.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: This done, he took the bride about the neck,

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And kiss’d her lips with such a clamorous smack

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: That at the parting all the church did echo.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And I, seeing this, came thence for very shame;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: And after me, I know, the rout is coming.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Such a mad marriage never was before.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Hark, hark! I hear the minstrels play.
[_Music plays._]
Enter Petruchio, Katherina, Bianca, Baptista, Hortensio, Grumio and Train.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Gentlemen and friends, I thank you for your pains:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I know you think to dine with me today,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And have prepar’d great store of wedding cheer

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But so it is, my haste doth call me hence,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And therefore here I mean to take my leave.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Is’t possible you will away tonight?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I must away today before night come.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Make it no wonder: if you knew my business,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You would entreat me rather go than stay.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And, honest company, I thank you all,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That have beheld me give away myself

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To this most patient, sweet, and virtuous wife.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Dine with my father, drink a health to me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For I must hence; and farewell to you all.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Let us entreat you stay till after dinner.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It may not be.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Let me entreat you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It cannot be.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Let me entreat you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I am content.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Are you content to stay?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I am content you shall entreat me stay;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But yet not stay, entreat me how you can.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Now, if you love me, stay.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Grumio, my horse!

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Ay, sir, they be ready; the oats have eaten the horses.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Nay, then,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Do what thou canst, I will not go today;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: No, nor tomorrow, not till I please myself.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: The door is open, sir; there lies your way;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: You may be jogging whiles your boots are green;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: For me, I’ll not be gone till I please myself.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: ’Tis like you’ll prove a jolly surly groom

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That take it on you at the first so roundly.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O Kate! content thee: prithee be not angry.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I will be angry: what hast thou to do?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Father, be quiet; he shall stay my leisure.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Ay, marry, sir, now it begins to work.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Gentlemen, forward to the bridal dinner:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I see a woman may be made a fool,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If she had not a spirit to resist.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: They shall go forward, Kate, at thy command.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Obey the bride, you that attend on her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go to the feast, revel and domineer,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Carouse full measure to her maidenhead,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Be mad and merry, or go hang yourselves:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But for my bonny Kate, she must with me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, look not big, nor stamp, nor stare, nor fret;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will be master of what is mine own.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She is my goods, my chattels; she is my house,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My household stuff, my field, my barn,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My horse, my ox, my ass, my anything;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And here she stands, touch her whoever dare;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll bring mine action on the proudest he

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That stops my way in Padua. Grumio,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Draw forth thy weapon; we are beset with thieves;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Rescue thy mistress, if thou be a man.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Fear not, sweet wench; they shall not touch thee, Kate;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll buckler thee against a million.
[_Exeunt Petruchio, Katherina and Grumio._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Nay, let them go, a couple of quiet ones.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Went they not quickly, I should die with laughing.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of all mad matches, never was the like.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Mistress, what’s your opinion of your sister?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: That, being mad herself, she’s madly mated.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I warrant him, Petruchio is Kated.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Neighbours and friends, though bride and bridegroom wants

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For to supply the places at the table,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: You know there wants no junkets at the feast.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Lucentio, you shall supply the bridegroom’s place;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And let Bianca take her sister’s room.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Shall sweet Bianca practise how to bride it?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: She shall, Lucentio. Come, gentlemen, let’s go.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A hall in Petruchio’s country house.

lines.text: Enter Grumio.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Fie, fie on all tired jades, on all mad masters, and all foul ways! Was

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: ever man so beaten? Was ever man so ray’d? Was ever man so weary? I am

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: sent before to make a fire, and they are coming after to warm them.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Now, were not I a little pot and soon hot, my very lips might freeze to

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: my teeth, my tongue to the roof of my mouth, my heart in my belly, ere

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I should come by a fire to thaw me. But I with blowing the fire shall

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: warm myself; for, considering the weather, a taller man than I will

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: take cold. Holla, ho! Curtis!
Enter Curtis.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Who is that calls so coldly?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: A piece of ice: if thou doubt it, thou mayst slide from my shoulder to

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: my heel with no greater a run but my head and my neck. A fire, good

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Curtis.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Is my master and his wife coming, Grumio?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: O, ay! Curtis, ay; and therefore fire, fire; cast on no water.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Is she so hot a shrew as she’s reported?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: She was, good Curtis, before this frost; but thou knowest winter tames

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: man, woman, and beast; for it hath tamed my old master, and my new

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: mistress, and myself, fellow Curtis.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Away, you three-inch fool! I am no beast.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Am I but three inches? Why, thy horn is a foot; and so long am I at the

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: least. But wilt thou make a fire, or shall I complain on thee to our

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: mistress, whose hand,—she being now at hand,— thou shalt soon feel, to

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: thy cold comfort, for being slow in thy hot office?

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: I prithee, good Grumio, tell me, how goes the world?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: A cold world, Curtis, in every office but thine; and therefore fire. Do

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: thy duty, and have thy duty, for my master and mistress are almost

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: frozen to death.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: There’s fire ready; and therefore, good Grumio, the news.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Why, ‘Jack boy! ho, boy!’ and as much news as wilt thou.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Come, you are so full of cony-catching.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Why, therefore, fire; for I have caught extreme cold. Where’s the cook?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Is supper ready, the house trimmed, rushes strewed, cobwebs swept, the

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: servingmen in their new fustian, their white stockings, and every

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: officer his wedding-garment on? Be the Jacks fair within, the Jills

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: fair without, and carpets laid, and everything in order?

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: All ready; and therefore, I pray thee, news.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: First, know my horse is tired; my master and mistress fallen out.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: How?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Out of their saddles into the dirt; and thereby hangs a tale.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Let’s ha’t, good Grumio.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Lend thine ear.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Here.
[_Striking him._]

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: There.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: This ’tis to feel a tale, not to hear a tale.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: And therefore ’tis called a sensible tale; and this cuff was but to

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: knock at your ear and beseech listening. Now I begin: _Imprimis_, we

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: came down a foul hill, my master riding behind my mistress,—

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Both of one horse?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: What’s that to thee?

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Why, a horse.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Tell thou the tale: but hadst thou not crossed me, thou shouldst have

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: heard how her horse fell, and she under her horse; thou shouldst have

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: heard in how miry a place, how she was bemoiled; how he left her with

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: the horse upon her; how he beat me because her horse stumbled; how she

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: waded through the dirt to pluck him off me: how he swore; how she

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: prayed, that never prayed before; how I cried; how the horses ran away;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: how her bridle was burst; how I lost my crupper; with many things of

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: worthy memory, which now shall die in oblivion, and thou return

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: unexperienced to thy grave.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: By this reckoning he is more shrew than she.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Ay; and that thou and the proudest of you all shall find when he comes

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: home. But what talk I of this? Call forth Nathaniel, Joseph, Nicholas,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Philip, Walter, Sugarsop, and the rest; let their heads be sleekly

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: combed, their blue coats brush’d and their garters of an indifferent

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: knit; let them curtsy with their left legs, and not presume to touch a

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: hair of my master’s horse-tail till they kiss their hands. Are they all

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: ready?

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: They are.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Call them forth.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Do you hear? ho! You must meet my master to countenance my mistress.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Why, she hath a face of her own.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Who knows not that?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Thou, it seems, that calls for company to countenance her.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: I call them forth to credit her.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Why, she comes to borrow nothing of them.
Enter four or five Servants.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Welcome home, Grumio!

lines.speaker: PHILIP
lines.text: How now, Grumio!

lines.speaker: JOSEPH
lines.text: What, Grumio!

lines.speaker: NICHOLAS
lines.text: Fellow Grumio!

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: How now, old lad!

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Welcome, you; how now, you; what, you; fellow, you; and thus much for

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: greeting. Now, my spruce companions, is all ready, and all things neat?

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: All things is ready. How near is our master?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: E’en at hand, alighted by this; and therefore be not,—

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Cock’s passion, silence! I hear my master.
Enter Petruchio and Katherina.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where be these knaves? What! no man at door

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To hold my stirrup nor to take my horse?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where is Nathaniel, Gregory, Philip?—

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: Here, here, sir; here, sir.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here, sir! here, sir! here, sir! here, sir!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You logger-headed and unpolish’d grooms!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What, no attendance? no regard? no duty?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where is the foolish knave I sent before?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Here, sir; as foolish as I was before.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You peasant swain! you whoreson malt-horse drudge!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Did I not bid thee meet me in the park,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And bring along these rascal knaves with thee?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Nathaniel’s coat, sir, was not fully made,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: And Gabriel’s pumps were all unpink’d i’ the heel;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: There was no link to colour Peter’s hat,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: And Walter’s dagger was not come from sheathing;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: There was none fine but Adam, Ralph, and Gregory;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: The rest were ragged, old, and beggarly;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Yet, as they are, here are they come to meet you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go, rascals, go and fetch my supper in.
[_Exeunt some of the Servants._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where is the life that late I led?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where are those—?  Sit down, Kate, and welcome.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Food, food, food, food!
Re-enter Servants with supper.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, when, I say?—Nay, good sweet Kate, be merry.—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Off with my boots, you rogues! you villains! when?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It was the friar of orders grey,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As he forth walked on his way:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Out, you rogue! you pluck my foot awry:
[_Strikes him._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Take that, and mend the plucking off the other.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Be merry, Kate. Some water, here; what, ho!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where’s my spaniel Troilus? Sirrah, get you hence

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And bid my cousin Ferdinand come hither:
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: One, Kate, that you must kiss and be acquainted with.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where are my slippers? Shall I have some water?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, Kate, and wash, and welcome heartily.—
[_Servant lets the ewer fall. Petruchio strikes him._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You whoreson villain! will you let it fall?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Patience, I pray you; ’twas a fault unwilling.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A whoreson, beetle-headed, flap-ear’d knave!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, Kate, sit down; I know you have a stomach.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Will you give thanks, sweet Kate, or else shall I?—

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What’s this? Mutton?

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Who brought it?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: I.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Tis burnt; and so is all the meat.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What dogs are these! Where is the rascal cook?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How durst you, villains, bring it from the dresser,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And serve it thus to me that love it not?
[_Throws the meat, etc., at them._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: There, take it to you, trenchers, cups, and all.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You heedless joltheads and unmanner’d slaves!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What! do you grumble? I’ll be with you straight.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I pray you, husband, be not so disquiet;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: The meat was well, if you were so contented.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I tell thee, Kate, ’twas burnt and dried away,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And I expressly am forbid to touch it;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For it engenders choler, planteth anger;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And better ’twere that both of us did fast,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Since, of ourselves, ourselves are choleric,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Than feed it with such over-roasted flesh.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Be patient; tomorrow ’t shall be mended.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And for this night we’ll fast for company:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, I will bring thee to thy bridal chamber.
[_Exeunt Petruchio, Katherina and Curtis._]

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Peter, didst ever see the like?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: He kills her in her own humour.
Re-enter Curtis.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Where is he?

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: In her chamber, making a sermon of continency to her;

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: And rails, and swears, and rates, that she, poor soul,

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Knows not which way to stand, to look, to speak,

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: And sits as one new risen from a dream.

lines.speaker: CURTIS
lines.text: Away, away! for he is coming hither.
[_Exeunt._]
Re-enter Petruchio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thus have I politicly begun my reign,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And ’tis my hope to end successfully.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My falcon now is sharp and passing empty.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And till she stoop she must not be full-gorg’d,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For then she never looks upon her lure.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Another way I have to man my haggard,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To make her come, and know her keeper’s call,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That is, to watch her, as we watch these kites

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That bate and beat, and will not be obedient.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She eat no meat today, nor none shall eat;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Last night she slept not, nor tonight she shall not;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As with the meat, some undeserved fault

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll find about the making of the bed;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And here I’ll fling the pillow, there the bolster,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: This way the coverlet, another way the sheets;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Ay, and amid this hurly I intend

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: That all is done in reverend care of her;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And, in conclusion, she shall watch all night:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And if she chance to nod I’ll rail and brawl,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And with the clamour keep her still awake.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: This is a way to kill a wife with kindness;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And thus I’ll curb her mad and headstrong humour.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: He that knows better how to tame a shrew,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now let him speak; ’tis charity to show.
[_Exit._]
Enter Tranio and Hortensio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Is ’t possible, friend Licio, that Mistress Bianca

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Doth fancy any other but Lucentio?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I tell you, sir, she bears me fair in hand.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sir, to satisfy you in what I have said,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Stand by and mark the manner of his teaching.
[_They stand aside._]
Enter Bianca and Lucentio.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Now, mistress, profit you in what you read?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: What, master, read you? First resolve me that.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I read that I profess, _The Art to Love_.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: And may you prove, sir, master of your art!

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: While you, sweet dear, prove mistress of my heart.
[_They retire._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Quick proceeders, marry! Now tell me, I pray,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: You that durst swear that your Mistress Bianca

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Lov’d none in the world so well as Lucentio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: O despiteful love! unconstant womankind!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I tell thee, Licio, this is wonderful.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Mistake no more; I am not Licio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Nor a musician as I seem to be;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: But one that scorn to live in this disguise

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For such a one as leaves a gentleman

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And makes a god of such a cullion:

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Know, sir, that I am call’d Hortensio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Signior Hortensio, I have often heard

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of your entire affection to Bianca;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And since mine eyes are witness of her lightness,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I will with you, if you be so contented,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Forswear Bianca and her love for ever.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: See, how they kiss and court! Signior Lucentio,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Here is my hand, and here I firmly vow

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Never to woo her more, but do forswear her,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: As one unworthy all the former favours

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That I have fondly flatter’d her withal.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And here I take the like unfeigned oath,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Never to marry with her though she would entreat;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Fie on her! See how beastly she doth court him!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Would all the world but he had quite forsworn!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For me, that I may surely keep mine oath,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I will be married to a wealthy widow

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Ere three days pass, which hath as long lov’d me

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: As I have lov’d this proud disdainful haggard.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And so farewell, Signior Lucentio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Kindness in women, not their beauteous looks,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Shall win my love; and so I take my leave,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: In resolution as I swore before.
[_Exit Hortensio. Lucentio and Bianca advance._]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Mistress Bianca, bless you with such grace

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As ’longeth to a lover’s blessed case!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Nay, I have ta’en you napping, gentle love,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And have forsworn you with Hortensio.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Tranio, you jest; but have you both forsworn me?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Mistress, we have.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Then we are rid of Licio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I’ faith, he’ll have a lusty widow now,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That shall be woo’d and wedded in a day.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: God give him joy!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Ay, and he’ll tame her.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: He says so, Tranio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Faith, he is gone unto the taming-school.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: The taming-school! What, is there such a place?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Ay, mistress; and Petruchio is the master,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That teacheth tricks eleven and twenty long,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To tame a shrew and charm her chattering tongue.
Enter Biondello, running.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: O master, master! I have watch’d so long

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: That I am dog-weary; but at last I spied

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: An ancient angel coming down the hill

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Will serve the turn.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: What is he, Biondello?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Master, a mercatante or a pedant,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I know not what; but formal in apparel,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: In gait and countenance surely like a father.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And what of him, Tranio?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If he be credulous and trust my tale,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I’ll make him glad to seem Vincentio,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And give assurance to Baptista Minola,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As if he were the right Vincentio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Take in your love, and then let me alone.
[_Exeunt Lucentio and Bianca._]
Enter a Pedant.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: God save you, sir!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And you, sir! you are welcome.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Travel you far on, or are you at the farthest?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Sir, at the farthest for a week or two;

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: But then up farther, and as far as Rome;

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: And so to Tripoli, if God lend me life.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: What countryman, I pray?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Of Mantua.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Of Mantua, sir?  Marry, God forbid,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And come to Padua, careless of your life!

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: My life, sir! How, I pray? for that goes hard.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis death for anyone in Mantua

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To come to Padua. Know you not the cause?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Your ships are stay’d at Venice; and the Duke,—

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: For private quarrel ’twixt your Duke and him,—

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Hath publish’d and proclaim’d it openly.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis marvel, but that you are but newly come

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: You might have heard it else proclaim’d about.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Alas, sir! it is worse for me than so;

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: For I have bills for money by exchange

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: From Florence, and must here deliver them.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Well, sir, to do you courtesy,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: This will I do, and this I will advise you:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: First, tell me, have you ever been at Pisa?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Ay, sir, in Pisa have I often been,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Pisa renowned for grave citizens.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Among them know you one Vincentio?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: I know him not, but I have heard of him,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: A merchant of incomparable wealth.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: He is my father, sir; and, sooth to say,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: In countenance somewhat doth resemble you.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: As much as an apple doth an oyster, and all one.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To save your life in this extremity,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: This favour will I do you for his sake;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And think it not the worst of all your fortunes

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: That you are like to Sir Vincentio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: His name and credit shall you undertake,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: And in my house you shall be friendly lodg’d;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Look that you take upon you as you should!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: You understand me, sir; so shall you stay

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Till you have done your business in the city.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: If this be courtesy, sir, accept of it.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: O, sir, I do; and will repute you ever

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: The patron of my life and liberty.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Then go with me to make the matter good.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: This, by the way, I let you understand:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: My father is here look’d for every day

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: To pass assurance of a dower in marriage

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Twixt me and one Baptista’s daughter here:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: In all these circumstances I’ll instruct you.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Go with me to clothe you as becomes you.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Katherina and Grumio.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: No, no, forsooth; I dare not for my life.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: The more my wrong, the more his spite appears.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What, did he marry me to famish me?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Beggars that come unto my father’s door

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Upon entreaty have a present alms;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: If not, elsewhere they meet with charity;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But I, who never knew how to entreat,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Nor never needed that I should entreat,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Am starv’d for meat, giddy for lack of sleep;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: With oaths kept waking, and with brawling fed.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And that which spites me more than all these wants,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: He does it under name of perfect love;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: As who should say, if I should sleep or eat

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: ’Twere deadly sickness, or else present death.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I prithee go and get me some repast;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I care not what, so it be wholesome food.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: What say you to a neat’s foot?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: ’Tis passing good; I prithee let me have it.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I fear it is too choleric a meat.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: How say you to a fat tripe finely broil’d?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I like it well; good Grumio, fetch it me.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I cannot tell; I fear ’tis choleric.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: What say you to a piece of beef and mustard?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A dish that I do love to feed upon.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Ay, but the mustard is too hot a little.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Why then the beef, and let the mustard rest.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Nay, then I will not: you shall have the mustard,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Or else you get no beef of Grumio.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Then both, or one, or anything thou wilt.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Why then the mustard without the beef.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Go, get thee gone, thou false deluding slave,
[_Beats him._]

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That feed’st me with the very name of meat.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Sorrow on thee and all the pack of you

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That triumph thus upon my misery!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Go, get thee gone, I say.
Enter Petruchio with a dish of meat; and Hortensio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How fares my Kate? What, sweeting, all amort?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Mistress, what cheer?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Faith, as cold as can be.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Pluck up thy spirits; look cheerfully upon me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here, love; thou seest how diligent I am,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To dress thy meat myself, and bring it thee:
[_Sets the dish on a table._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I am sure, sweet Kate, this kindness merits thanks.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What! not a word? Nay, then thou lov’st it not,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And all my pains is sorted to no proof.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here, take away this dish.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I pray you, let it stand.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The poorest service is repaid with thanks;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And so shall mine, before you touch the meat.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I thank you, sir.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Signior Petruchio, fie! you are to blame.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Come, Mistress Kate, I’ll bear you company.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Eat it up all, Hortensio, if thou lovest me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Much good do it unto thy gentle heart!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Kate, eat apace: and now, my honey love,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Will we return unto thy father’s house

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And revel it as bravely as the best,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: With silken coats and caps, and golden rings,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: With ruffs and cuffs and farthingales and things;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: With scarfs and fans and double change of bravery,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: With amber bracelets, beads, and all this knavery.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What! hast thou din’d? The tailor stays thy leisure,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To deck thy body with his ruffling treasure.
Enter Tailor.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, tailor, let us see these ornaments;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Lay forth the gown.—
Enter Haberdasher.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What news with you, sir?

lines.speaker: HABERDASHER
lines.text: Here is the cap your worship did bespeak.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, this was moulded on a porringer;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A velvet dish: fie, fie! ’tis lewd and filthy:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, ’tis a cockle or a walnut-shell,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A knack, a toy, a trick, a baby’s cap:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Away with it! come, let me have a bigger.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I’ll have no bigger; this doth fit the time,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And gentlewomen wear such caps as these.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: When you are gentle, you shall have one too,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And not till then.
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That will not be in haste.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Why, sir, I trust I may have leave to speak;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And speak I will. I am no child, no babe.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Your betters have endur’d me say my mind,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And if you cannot, best you stop your ears.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: My tongue will tell the anger of my heart,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Or else my heart, concealing it, will break;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And rather than it shall, I will be free

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Even to the uttermost, as I please, in words.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, thou say’st true; it is a paltry cap,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A custard-coffin, a bauble, a silken pie;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I love thee well in that thou lik’st it not.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Love me or love me not, I like the cap;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And it I will have, or I will have none.
[_Exit Haberdasher._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thy gown? Why, ay: come, tailor, let us see’t.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O mercy, God! what masquing stuff is here?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What’s this? A sleeve? ’Tis like a demi-cannon.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What, up and down, carv’d like an apple tart?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Here’s snip and nip and cut and slish and slash,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Like to a censer in a barber’s shop.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, what i’ devil’s name, tailor, call’st thou this?
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I see she’s like to have neither cap nor gown.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: You bid me make it orderly and well,

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: According to the fashion and the time.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Marry, and did; but if you be remember’d,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I did not bid you mar it to the time.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go, hop me over every kennel home,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For you shall hop without my custom, sir.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll none of it: hence! make your best of it.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I never saw a better fashion’d gown,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: More quaint, more pleasing, nor more commendable;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Belike you mean to make a puppet of me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, true; he means to make a puppet of thee.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: She says your worship means to make a puppet of her.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O monstrous arrogance! Thou liest, thou thread,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou thimble,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou yard, three-quarters, half-yard, quarter, nail!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thou flea, thou nit, thou winter-cricket thou!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Brav’d in mine own house with a skein of thread!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Away! thou rag, thou quantity, thou remnant,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Or I shall so be-mete thee with thy yard

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As thou shalt think on prating whilst thou liv’st!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I tell thee, I, that thou hast marr’d her gown.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: Your worship is deceiv’d: the gown is made

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: Just as my master had direction.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: Grumio gave order how it should be done.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I gave him no order; I gave him the stuff.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: But how did you desire it should be made?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Marry, sir, with needle and thread.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: But did you not request to have it cut?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Thou hast faced many things.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: I have.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Face not me. Thou hast braved many men; brave not me: I will neither be

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: fac’d nor brav’d. I say unto thee, I bid thy master cut out the gown;

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: but I did not bid him cut it to pieces: ergo, thou liest.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: Why, here is the note of the fashion to testify.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Read it.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: The note lies in ’s throat, if he say I said so.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: ’Imprimis, a loose-bodied gown.’

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Master, if ever I said loose-bodied gown, sew me in the skirts of it

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: and beat me to death with a bottom of brown thread; I said, a gown.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Proceed.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: ‘With a small compassed cape.’

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I confess the cape.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: ‘With a trunk sleeve.’

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I confess two sleeves.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: ‘The sleeves curiously cut.’

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Ay, there’s the villainy.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Error i’ the bill, sir; error i’ the bill. I commanded the sleeves

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: should be cut out, and sew’d up again; and that I’ll prove upon thee,

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: though thy little finger be armed in a thimble.

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: This is true that I say; and I had thee in place where thou shouldst

lines.speaker: TAILOR
lines.text: know it.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: I am for thee straight; take thou the bill, give me thy mete-yard, and

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: spare not me.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: God-a-mercy, Grumio! Then he shall have no odds.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Well, sir, in brief, the gown is not for me.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: You are i’ the right, sir; ’tis for my mistress.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go, take it up unto thy master’s use.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Villain, not for thy life! Take up my mistress’ gown for thy master’s

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: use!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, sir, what’s your conceit in that?

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: O, sir, the conceit is deeper than you think for.

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: Take up my mistress’ gown to his master’s use!

lines.speaker: GRUMIO
lines.text: O fie, fie, fie!
[_Aside_]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hortensio, say thou wilt see the tailor paid.
[_To Tailor._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go take it hence; be gone, and say no more.
[_Aside to Tailor._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Tailor, I’ll pay thee for thy gown tomorrow;

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Take no unkindness of his hasty words.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Away, I say! commend me to thy master.
[_Exit Tailor._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Well, come, my Kate; we will unto your father’s

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Even in these honest mean habiliments.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Our purses shall be proud, our garments poor

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For ’tis the mind that makes the body rich;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: So honour peereth in the meanest habit.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What, is the jay more precious than the lark

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Because his feathers are more beautiful?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Or is the adder better than the eel

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Because his painted skin contents the eye?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O no, good Kate; neither art thou the worse

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For this poor furniture and mean array.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: If thou account’st it shame, lay it on me;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And therefore frolic; we will hence forthwith,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To feast and sport us at thy father’s house.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go call my men, and let us straight to him;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And bring our horses unto Long-lane end;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: There will we mount, and thither walk on foot.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Let’s see; I think ’tis now some seven o’clock,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And well we may come there by dinner-time.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I dare assure you, sir, ’tis almost two,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And ’twill be supper-time ere you come there.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It shall be seven ere I go to horse.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Look what I speak, or do, or think to do,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You are still crossing it. Sirs, let ’t alone:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I will not go today; and ere I do,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It shall be what o’clock I say it is.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Why, so this gallant will command the sun.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Tranio and the Pedant dressed like Vincentio

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Sir, this is the house; please it you that I call?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Ay, what else? and, but I be deceived,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Signior Baptista may remember me,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Near twenty years ago in Genoa,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Where we were lodgers at the Pegasus.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis well; and hold your own, in any case,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: With such austerity as ’longeth to a father.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: I warrant you. But, sir, here comes your boy;

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: ’Twere good he were school’d.
Enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Fear you not him. Sirrah Biondello,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Now do your duty throughly, I advise you.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Imagine ’twere the right Vincentio.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Tut! fear not me.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: But hast thou done thy errand to Baptista?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I told him that your father was at Venice,

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: And that you look’d for him this day in Padua.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Th’art a tall fellow; hold thee that to drink.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Here comes Baptista. Set your countenance, sir.
Enter Baptista and Lucentio.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista, you are happily met.
[_To the Pedant_]

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Sir, this is the gentleman I told you of;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I pray you stand good father to me now;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Give me Bianca for my patrimony.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Soft, son!

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Sir, by your leave: having come to Padua

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: To gather in some debts, my son Lucentio

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Made me acquainted with a weighty cause

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Of love between your daughter and himself:

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: And,—for the good report I hear of you,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: And for the love he beareth to your daughter,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: And she to him,—to stay him not too long,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: I am content, in a good father’s care,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: To have him match’d; and, if you please to like

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: No worse than I, upon some agreement

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Me shall you find ready and willing

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: With one consent to have her so bestow’d;

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: For curious I cannot be with you,

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Signior Baptista, of whom I hear so well.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Sir, pardon me in what I have to say.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Your plainness and your shortness please me well.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Right true it is your son Lucentio here

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Doth love my daughter, and she loveth him,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Or both dissemble deeply their affections;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And therefore, if you say no more than this,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: That like a father you will deal with him,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And pass my daughter a sufficient dower,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: The match is made, and all is done:

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Your son shall have my daughter with consent.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: I thank you, sir. Where then do you know best

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: We be affied, and such assurance ta’en

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: As shall with either part’s agreement stand?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Not in my house, Lucentio, for you know

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Pitchers have ears, and I have many servants;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Besides, old Gremio is hearkening still,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And happily we might be interrupted.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Then at my lodging, and it like you:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: There doth my father lie; and there this night

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: We’ll pass the business privately and well.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Send for your daughter by your servant here;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: My boy shall fetch the scrivener presently.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: The worst is this, that at so slender warning

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: You are like to have a thin and slender pittance.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: It likes me well. Cambio, hie you home,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And bid Bianca make her ready straight;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And, if you will, tell what hath happened:

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Lucentio’s father is arriv’d in Padua,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And how she’s like to be Lucentio’s wife.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I pray the gods she may, with all my heart!

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Dally not with the gods, but get thee gone.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Signior Baptista, shall I lead the way?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Welcome! One mess is like to be your cheer;

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Come, sir; we will better it in Pisa.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I follow you.
[_Exeunt Tranio, Pedant and Baptista._]

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Cambio!

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: What say’st thou, Biondello?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: You saw my master wink and laugh upon you?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Biondello, what of that?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Faith, nothing; but has left me here behind to expound the meaning or

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: moral of his signs and tokens.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I pray thee moralize them.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Then thus: Baptista is safe, talking with the deceiving father of a

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: deceitful son.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And what of him?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: His daughter is to be brought by you to the supper.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: The old priest at Saint Luke’s church is at your command at all hours.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And what of all this?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I cannot tell, except they are busied about a counterfeit assurance.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Take your assurance of her, _cum privilegio ad imprimendum solum_; to

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: the church! take the priest, clerk, and some sufficient honest

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: witnesses. If this be not that you look for, I have more to say, But

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: bid Bianca farewell for ever and a day.
[_Going._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Hear’st thou, Biondello?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I cannot tarry: I knew a wench married in an afternoon as she went to

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: the garden for parsley to stuff a rabbit; and so may you, sir; and so

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: adieu, sir. My master hath appointed me to go to Saint Luke’s to bid

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: the priest be ready to come against you come with your appendix.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I may, and will, if she be so contented.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: She will be pleas’d; then wherefore should I doubt?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Hap what hap may, I’ll roundly go about her;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: It shall go hard if Cambio go without her:
[_Exit._]
Enter Petruchio, Katherina, Hortensio and Servants.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come on, i’ God’s name; once more toward our father’s.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Good Lord, how bright and goodly shines the moon!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: The moon! The sun; it is not moonlight now.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I say it is the moon that shines so bright.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I know it is the sun that shines so bright.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now by my mother’s son, and that’s myself,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: It shall be moon, or star, or what I list,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Or ere I journey to your father’s house.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go on and fetch our horses back again.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Evermore cross’d and cross’d; nothing but cross’d!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Say as he says, or we shall never go.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Forward, I pray, since we have come so far,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And be it moon, or sun, or what you please;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And if you please to call it a rush-candle,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Henceforth I vow it shall be so for me.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I say it is the moon.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I know it is the moon.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, then you lie; it is the blessed sun.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Then, God be bless’d, it is the blessed sun;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But sun it is not when you say it is not,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And the moon changes even as your mind.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What you will have it nam’d, even that it is,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And so it shall be so for Katherine.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Petruchio, go thy ways; the field is won.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Well, forward, forward! thus the bowl should run,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And not unluckily against the bias.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But, soft! Company is coming here.
Enter Vincentio, in a travelling dress.
[_To Vincentio_]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Good morrow, gentle mistress; where away?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Tell me, sweet Kate, and tell me truly too,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Hast thou beheld a fresher gentlewoman?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Such war of white and red within her cheeks!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What stars do spangle heaven with such beauty

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As those two eyes become that heavenly face?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Fair lovely maid, once more good day to thee.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sweet Kate, embrace her for her beauty’s sake.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: A will make the man mad, to make a woman of him.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Young budding virgin, fair and fresh and sweet,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Whither away, or where is thy abode?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Happy the parents of so fair a child;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Happier the man whom favourable stars

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Allot thee for his lovely bedfellow.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, how now, Kate! I hope thou art not mad:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: This is a man, old, wrinkled, faded, wither’d,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And not a maiden, as thou sayst he is.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Pardon, old father, my mistaking eyes,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That have been so bedazzled with the sun

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That everything I look on seemeth green:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Now I perceive thou art a reverend father;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Pardon, I pray thee, for my mad mistaking.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Do, good old grandsire, and withal make known

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Which way thou travellest: if along with us,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: We shall be joyful of thy company.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Fair sir, and you my merry mistress,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: That with your strange encounter much amaz’d me,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: My name is called Vincentio; my dwelling Pisa;

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: And bound I am to Padua, there to visit

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: A son of mine, which long I have not seen.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What is his name?

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Lucentio, gentle sir.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Happily met; the happier for thy son.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And now by law, as well as reverend age,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I may entitle thee my loving father:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The sister to my wife, this gentlewoman,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thy son by this hath married. Wonder not,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nor be not griev’d: she is of good esteem,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her dowry wealthy, and of worthy birth;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Beside, so qualified as may beseem

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The spouse of any noble gentleman.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Let me embrace with old Vincentio;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And wander we to see thy honest son,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Who will of thy arrival be full joyous.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: But is this true? or is it else your pleasure,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Like pleasant travellers, to break a jest

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Upon the company you overtake?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I do assure thee, father, so it is.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, go along, and see the truth hereof;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: For our first merriment hath made thee jealous.
[_Exeunt all but Hortensio._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Well, Petruchio, this has put me in heart.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Have to my widow! and if she be froward,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Then hast thou taught Hortensio to be untoward.
[_Exit._]
Enter on one side Biondello, Lucentio and Bianca; Gremio walking on other side.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Softly and swiftly, sir, for the priest is ready.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I fly, Biondello; but they may chance to need thee at home, therefore

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: leave us.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Nay, faith, I’ll see the church o’ your back; and then come back to my

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: master’s as soon as I can.
[_Exeunt Lucentio, Bianca and Biondello._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I marvel Cambio comes not all this while.
Enter Petruchio, Katherina, Vincentio and Attendants.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sir, here’s the door; this is Lucentio’s house:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: My father’s bears more toward the market-place;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Thither must I, and here I leave you, sir.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: You shall not choose but drink before you go.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: I think I shall command your welcome here,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: And by all likelihood some cheer is toward.
[_Knocks._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: They’re busy within; you were best knock louder.
Enter Pedant above, at a window.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: What’s he that knocks as he would beat down the gate?

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Is Signior Lucentio within, sir?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: He’s within, sir, but not to be spoken withal.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: What if a man bring him a hundred pound or two to make merry withal?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Keep your hundred pounds to yourself: he shall need none so long as I

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: live.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, I told you your son was well beloved in Padua. Do you hear, sir?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To leave frivolous circumstances, I pray you tell Signior Lucentio that

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: his father is come from Pisa, and is here at the door to speak with

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Thou liest: his father is come from Padua, and here looking out at the

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: window.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Art thou his father?

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Ay, sir; so his mother says, if I may believe her.
[_To Vincentio_]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, how now, gentleman! why, this is flat knavery to

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: take upon you another man’s name.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Lay hands on the villain: I believe a means to cozen somebody in this

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: city under my countenance.
Re-enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I have seen them in the church together: God send ’em good shipping!

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: But who is here? Mine old master, Vincentio! Now we are undone and

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: brought to nothing.
[_Seeing Biondello._]

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Come hither, crack-hemp.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I hope I may choose, sir.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
