lines.text: Come hither, you rogue. What, have you forgot me?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Forgot you! No, sir: I could not forget you, for I never saw you before

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: in all my life.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: What, you notorious villain! didst thou never see thy master’s father,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Vincentio?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: What, my old worshipful old master? Yes, marry, sir; see where he looks

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: out of the window.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Is’t so, indeed?
[_He beats Biondello._]

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Help, help, help! here’s a madman will murder me.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Help, son! help, Signior Baptista!
[_Exit from the window._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Prithee, Kate, let’s stand aside and see the end of this controversy.
[_They retire._]
Re-enter Pedant, below; Baptista, Tranio and Servants.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Sir, what are you that offer to beat my servant?

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: What am I, sir! nay, what are you, sir? O immortal gods! O fine

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: villain! A silken doublet, a velvet hose, a scarlet cloak, and a

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: copatain hat! O, I am undone! I am undone! While I play the good

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: husband at home, my son and my servant spend all at the university.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: How now! what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: What, is the man lunatic?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Sir, you seem a sober ancient gentleman by your habit, but your words

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: show you a madman. Why, sir, what ’cerns it you if I wear pearl and

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: gold? I thank my good father, I am able to maintain it.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Thy father! O villain! he is a sailmaker in Bergamo.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: You mistake, sir; you mistake, sir. Pray, what do you think is his

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: name?

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: His name! As if I knew not his name! I have brought him up ever since

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: he was three years old, and his name is Tranio.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Away, away, mad ass! His name is Lucentio; and he is mine only son, and

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: heir to the lands of me, Signior Vincentio.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Lucentio! O, he hath murdered his master! Lay hold on him, I charge

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: you, in the Duke’s name. O, my son, my son! Tell me, thou villain,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: where is my son, Lucentio?

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Call forth an officer.
Enter one with an Officer.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Carry this mad knave to the gaol. Father Baptista, I charge you see

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: that he be forthcoming.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Carry me to the gaol!

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Stay, officer; he shall not go to prison.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Talk not, Signior Gremio; I say he shall go to prison.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Take heed, Signior Baptista, lest you be cony-catched in this business;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: I dare swear this is the right Vincentio.

lines.speaker: PEDANT
lines.text: Swear if thou darest.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Nay, I dare not swear it.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Then thou wert best say that I am not Lucentio.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Yes, I know thee to be Signior Lucentio.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Away with the dotard! to the gaol with him!

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Thus strangers may be haled and abus’d: O monstrous villain!
Re-enter Biondello, with Lucentio and Bianca.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: O! we are spoiled; and yonder he is: deny him, forswear him, or else we

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: are all undone.
[_Kneeling._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Pardon, sweet father.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Lives my sweetest son?
[_Biondello, Tranio and Pedant run out._]
[_Kneeling._]

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Pardon, dear father.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: How hast thou offended?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Where is Lucentio?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Here’s Lucentio,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Right son to the right Vincentio;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: That have by marriage made thy daughter mine,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: While counterfeit supposes blear’d thine eyne.

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Here ’s packing, with a witness, to deceive us all!

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Where is that damned villain, Tranio,

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: That fac’d and brav’d me in this matter so?

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Why, tell me, is not this my Cambio?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Cambio is chang’d into Lucentio.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Love wrought these miracles. Bianca’s love

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Made me exchange my state with Tranio,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: While he did bear my countenance in the town;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And happily I have arriv’d at the last

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Unto the wished haven of my bliss.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: What Tranio did, myself enforc’d him to;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Then pardon him, sweet father, for my sake.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: I’ll slit the villain’s nose that would have sent me to the gaol.
[_To Lucentio._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: But do you hear, sir? Have you married my daughter

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: without asking my good will?

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Fear not, Baptista; we will content you, go to: but I will in, to be

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: revenged for this villainy.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: And I to sound the depth of this knavery.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Look not pale, Bianca; thy father will not frown.
[_Exeunt Lucentio and Bianca._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: My cake is dough, but I’ll in among the rest;

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Out of hope of all but my share of the feast.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Petruchio and Katherina advance.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Husband, let’s follow to see the end of this ado.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: First kiss me, Kate, and we will.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What! in the midst of the street?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What! art thou ashamed of me?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: No, sir; God forbid; but ashamed to kiss.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, then, let’s home again. Come, sirrah, let’s away.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Nay, I will give thee a kiss: now pray thee, love, stay.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Is not this well? Come, my sweet Kate:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Better once than never, for never too late.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Baptista, Vincentio, Gremio, the Pedant, Lucentio, Bianca, Petruchio, Katherina, Hortensio and Widow. Tranio, Biondello and Grumio and Others, attending.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: At last, though long, our jarring notes agree:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And time it is when raging war is done,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: To smile at ’scapes and perils overblown.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: My fair Bianca, bid my father welcome,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: While I with self-same kindness welcome thine.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Brother Petruchio, sister Katherina,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: And thou, Hortensio, with thy loving widow,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Feast with the best, and welcome to my house:

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: My banquet is to close our stomachs up,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: After our great good cheer. Pray you, sit down;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: For now we sit to chat as well as eat.
[_They sit at table._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nothing but sit and sit, and eat and eat!

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Padua affords this kindness, son Petruchio.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Padua affords nothing but what is kind.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: For both our sakes I would that word were true.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Now, for my life, Hortensio fears his widow.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Then never trust me if I be afeard.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: You are very sensible, and yet you miss my sense:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I mean Hortensio is afeard of you.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: He that is giddy thinks the world turns round.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Roundly replied.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Mistress, how mean you that?

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Thus I conceive by him.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Conceives by me! How likes Hortensio that?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: My widow says thus she conceives her tale.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Very well mended. Kiss him for that, good widow.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: ’He that is giddy thinks the world turns round’:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I pray you tell me what you meant by that.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Your husband, being troubled with a shrew,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Measures my husband’s sorrow by his woe;

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: And now you know my meaning.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A very mean meaning.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Right, I mean you.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And I am mean, indeed, respecting you.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To her, Kate!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To her, widow!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A hundred marks, my Kate does put her down.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: That’s my office.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Spoke like an officer: ha’ to thee, lad.
[_Drinks to Hortensio._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: How likes Gremio these quick-witted folks?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Believe me, sir, they butt together well.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Head and butt! An hasty-witted body

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Would say your head and butt were head and horn.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: Ay, mistress bride, hath that awaken’d you?

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Ay, but not frighted me; therefore I’ll sleep again.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, that you shall not; since you have begun,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Have at you for a bitter jest or two.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Am I your bird? I mean to shift my bush,

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: And then pursue me as you draw your bow.

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: You are welcome all.
[_Exeunt Bianca, Katherina and Widow._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: She hath prevented me. Here, Signior Tranio;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: This bird you aim’d at, though you hit her not:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Therefore a health to all that shot and miss’d.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: O, sir! Lucentio slipp’d me like his greyhound,

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: Which runs himself, and catches for his master.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A good swift simile, but something currish.

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis well, sir, that you hunted for yourself:

lines.speaker: TRANIO
lines.text: ’Tis thought your deer does hold you at a bay.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: O ho, Petruchio! Tranio hits you now.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I thank thee for that gird, good Tranio.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Confess, confess; hath he not hit you here?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A has a little gall’d me, I confess;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And as the jest did glance away from me,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Tis ten to one it maim’d you two outright.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now, in good sadness, son Petruchio,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: I think thou hast the veriest shrew of all.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Well, I say no; and therefore, for assurance,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Let’s each one send unto his wife,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And he whose wife is most obedient,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: To come at first when he doth send for her,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Shall win the wager which we will propose.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Content. What’s the wager?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Twenty crowns.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Twenty crowns!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I’ll venture so much of my hawk or hound,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: But twenty times so much upon my wife.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: A hundred then.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Content.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: A match! ’tis done.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Who shall begin?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: That will I.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Go, Biondello, bid your mistress come to me.

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: I go.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Son, I’ll be your half, Bianca comes.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I’ll have no halves; I’ll bear it all myself.
Re-enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: How now! what news?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: Sir, my mistress sends you word

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: That she is busy and she cannot come.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: How! She’s busy, and she cannot come!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Is that an answer?

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Ay, and a kind one too:

lines.speaker: GREMIO
lines.text: Pray God, sir, your wife send you not a worse.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I hope better.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Sirrah Biondello, go and entreat my wife

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: To come to me forthwith.
[_Exit Biondello._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: O, ho! entreat her!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, then she must needs come.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I am afraid, sir,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Do what you can, yours will not be entreated.
Re-enter Biondello.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Now, where’s my wife?

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: She says you have some goodly jest in hand:

lines.speaker: BIONDELLO
lines.text: She will not come; she bids you come to her.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Worse and worse; she will not come! O vile,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Intolerable, not to be endur’d!

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Sirrah Grumio, go to your mistress,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Say I command her come to me.
[_Exit Grumio._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: I know her answer.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: She will not.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: The fouler fortune mine, and there an end.
Re-enter Katherina.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now, by my holidame, here comes Katherina!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What is your will sir, that you send for me?

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Where is your sister, and Hortensio’s wife?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: They sit conferring by the parlour fire.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Go fetch them hither; if they deny to come,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Swinge me them soundly forth unto their husbands.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Away, I say, and bring them hither straight.
[_Exit Katherina._]

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Here is a wonder, if you talk of a wonder.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: And so it is. I wonder what it bodes.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Marry, peace it bodes, and love, and quiet life,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: An awful rule, and right supremacy;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And, to be short, what not that’s sweet and happy.

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Now fair befall thee, good Petruchio!

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: The wager thou hast won; and I will add

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Unto their losses twenty thousand crowns;

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: Another dowry to another daughter,

lines.speaker: BAPTISTA
lines.text: For she is chang’d, as she had never been.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Nay, I will win my wager better yet,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And show more sign of her obedience,

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Her new-built virtue and obedience.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: See where she comes, and brings your froward wives

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: As prisoners to her womanly persuasion.
Re-enter Katherina with Bianca and Widow.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Katherine, that cap of yours becomes you not:

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Off with that bauble, throw it underfoot.
[_Katherina pulls off her cap and throws it down._]

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Lord, let me never have a cause to sigh

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Till I be brought to such a silly pass!

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: Fie! what a foolish duty call you this?

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: I would your duty were as foolish too;

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: The wisdom of your duty, fair Bianca,

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Hath cost me a hundred crowns since supper-time!

lines.speaker: BIANCA
lines.text: The more fool you for laying on my duty.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Katherine, I charge thee, tell these headstrong women

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: What duty they do owe their lords and husbands.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Come, come, you’re mocking; we will have no telling.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come on, I say; and first begin with her.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: She shall not.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: I say she shall: and first begin with her.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Fie, fie! unknit that threatening unkind brow,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And dart not scornful glances from those eyes

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To wound thy lord, thy king, thy governor:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: It blots thy beauty as frosts do bite the meads,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Confounds thy fame as whirlwinds shake fair buds,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And in no sense is meet or amiable.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: A woman mov’d is like a fountain troubled,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Muddy, ill-seeming, thick, bereft of beauty;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And while it is so, none so dry or thirsty

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Will deign to sip or touch one drop of it.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Thy husband is thy lord, thy life, thy keeper,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Thy head, thy sovereign; one that cares for thee,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And for thy maintenance commits his body

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To painful labour both by sea and land,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To watch the night in storms, the day in cold,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Whilst thou liest warm at home, secure and safe;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And craves no other tribute at thy hands

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But love, fair looks, and true obedience;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Too little payment for so great a debt.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Such duty as the subject owes the prince,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Even such a woman oweth to her husband;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And when she is froward, peevish, sullen, sour,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And not obedient to his honest will,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: What is she but a foul contending rebel

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And graceless traitor to her loving lord?—

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: I am asham’d that women are so simple

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To offer war where they should kneel for peace,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Or seek for rule, supremacy, and sway,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: When they are bound to serve, love, and obey.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Why are our bodies soft and weak and smooth,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Unapt to toil and trouble in the world,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But that our soft conditions and our hearts

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Should well agree with our external parts?

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Come, come, you froward and unable worms!

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: My mind hath been as big as one of yours,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: My heart as great, my reason haply more,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: To bandy word for word and frown for frown;

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: But now I see our lances are but straws,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Our strength as weak, our weakness past compare,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: That seeming to be most which we indeed least are.

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: Then vail your stomachs, for it is no boot,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: And place your hands below your husband’s foot:

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: In token of which duty, if he please,

lines.speaker: KATHERINA
lines.text: My hand is ready; may it do him ease.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Why, there’s a wench! Come on, and kiss me, Kate.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: Well, go thy ways, old lad, for thou shalt ha’t.

lines.speaker: VINCENTIO
lines.text: ’Tis a good hearing when children are toward.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: But a harsh hearing when women are froward.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: Come, Kate, we’ll to bed.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: We three are married, but you two are sped.

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: ’Twas I won the wager,
[_To Lucentio._]

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: though you hit the white;

lines.speaker: PETRUCHIO
lines.text: And being a winner, God give you good night!
[_Exeunt Petruchio and Katherina._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIO
lines.text: Now go thy ways; thou hast tam’d a curst shrew.

lines.speaker: LUCENTIO
lines.text: ’Tis a wonder, by your leave, she will be tam’d so.
[_Exeunt._]
